summary: Not as a reversal signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, a bottom wick did the same as random on 4h and daily. On 1h it beat random only at 20 candles, and only because it fires in volatile candles. The result that holds up runs the other way: after a top wick started, price rose more than after random candles on 1h and 4h, so shorting it did worse than random.

verdicts.use: Shorting a top wick (signal start, threshold 1)
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h and 4h. Price kept rising after top wicks, and this holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

verdicts.use: Buying a bottom wick (signal start, threshold 1)
verdicts.text: Fragile on 1h: it beat random at 20 candles only and was the same as random at 10, 50 and 100. It fires in volatile candles, so price moved more after them in a window that rose. That is timing, not direction.

verdicts.use: Shorting while a top wick level holds
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h at 10 and 20 candles, and the same as random at 50 and 100. On 4h it was the same as random.

verdicts.use: Buying at threshold 2, or while a bottom wick level holds
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h and 4h, both as a fresh signal at threshold 2 and as a level held for 200 bars.

notes: Shorting at the start of a top wick on 1h gave 1,497 entries in 1,163 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.60% behind random entries, well outside the luck band. On 4h the gap was 2.26%, and on SOL 4h it reached 4.37%. These candles are volatile ones, so part of the gap may come from when they fire rather than from the wick itself.

The regimes split on 4h. On 1h the top wick short did worse than random in uptrends (0.69%) and in downtrends (0.36%). On 4h it did 2.13% worse in uptrends, but in downtrends it was the same as random. On daily the result sits inside the luck band.

Buying the start of a bottom wick on 1h beat random by 0.32%, just above the band's top of 0.22%, and only at 20 candles. The gap comes from uptrends, where it beat random by 0.34%; in downtrends it showed nothing. SOL carried it with 1.07% at every horizon. BTC did 0.20% worse, but only because of signals on Jun 12–15, 2022. These are volatile candles in a window that rose, so price moved more after them; the wick did not pick direction.

On 4h the bottom wick start was the same as random pooled, at 0.70% inside the band. The regimes pull apart: it beat random by 1.23% in uptrends and did 1.75% worse in downtrends. The downtrend loss rests on signals on Nov 7–9, 2022, during the FTX collapse, and without them it is the same as random. SOL's 1.80% on 4h rests on two signals on Feb 19–20, 2021.

Threshold 1 fires about five times as often as threshold 2 on 1h, and threshold 2 was the same as random on 1h and 4h. Holding a bottom wick level for 200 bars gave 37,470 entries on 1h but only 287 separate moves, and they landed at 0.03%, the same as random. Holding a top wick level did 0.34% worse than random on 1h. In downtrends that result rests on signals on Jan 2–4, 2023. Most daily cells have too few moves to judge.

For a short bot, a fresh top wick on 1h or 4h is a reason to leave the setting out: price rose more after it than after random candles. For a long DCA bot, a bottom wick adds no direction. On 1h in uptrends it marks candles after which price moved further, which matters for where you set the take profit and DCA steps. In 4h downtrends the same entries did worse around the FTX collapse, so pair it with a trend filter instead of letting it open deals alone.
